tools.name: find_credits
tools.description: Answer "what free credits / free tier / startup program can I get for X". Ranked, verified offers matching a need such as "free speech to text credits", "GPU for a bootstrapped startup" or "student LLM API credits". Each result has credit_value, eligibility, how_to_claim, claim_url, source_url, sour

tools.name: trending
tools.description: Offers people are actually claiming (clicks on the claim link, one per visitor per day) or voting "worked for me", over the last 7 days or all time. Counts are real and never seeded; when nothing has been claimed yet the list is empty and says so.

tools.name: get_offer
tools.description: Full record for one Perq offer by id (e.g. "deepgram-200-credit"), including source quote, last_verified, recorded changes and packs that contain it.

tools.name: list_packs
tools.description: Curated bundles of offers (e.g. AI startup launch pack, LLM API free tier pack, voice AI pack) with each pack's headline and up-to total where one is computed.

tools.name: get_pack
tools.description: One curated pack by slug with every offer in it and how its up-to total was computed (which offers counted and why others did not).

tools.name: recently_changed
tools.description: Offers added, updated (value, eligibility, claim steps) or closed in the last N days (dates in America/New_York).

tools.name: subscribe
tools.description: Get newly verified offers before they are public on https://perq.sh (about 24h early), plus closures and changes. Give either email (a person: we send a confirmation link, then a digest only on days with something new) or webhook_url (an agent: https only, public hosts only; each new offer is POSTed

tools.name: early_offers
tools.description: Offers that are verified but not public yet (embargoed, each with public_after), plus new, changed and closed offer events from the last 30 days, filtered by the subscription topics. Needs the private feed token from subscribe (webhook) or from the email confirmation page.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "subscribe" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: subscribe · Private data: get_offer, subscribe, early_offers · Public sink: subscribe, early_offers.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: subscribe · Private data: get_offer, subscribe, early_offers · Public sink: subscribe, early_offers

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
